messages:
Anya: Quick sync — we've got repeated onboarding flakes where tiny models (seq_len ~64) get benched with avg seqlen ~1024 and so runtime batching overwhelms latency SLAs. Options on the table: seqlen-aware admit metadata, runtime dynamic batch-splitting, or preflight 'stretch' runs to mimic production shapes. thoughts? cc @Siva @PJ
Siva: I lean toward seqlen-aware admit metadata. Dynamic splitting is powerful but touches runtime KV continuity and complicates tracing.
PJ: Could be as simple as adding a pad_profile in the model manifest (short|prod). Bench would fold that into sampling. Minimal ML infra change.
Marcus: Fake-long/preflight runs worry me — raises bench cost and increases onboarding time. Not great for self-serve.
Anya: Example manifest idea:
```
model_manifest:
  name: "tiny-chat"
  pad_profile: "short"
  max_seq: 64
```
Bench uses pad_profile to synthesize realistic batch shapes and inform admit checks.
Siva: Need backwards compat: if pad_profile missing, default to 'prod'. Also add validation in intake to reject nonsensical combos (max_seq > hardware limit etc.).
PJ: On the ops side: if we tag models as 'short' we might want route-level SLO hints (e.g., allow slightly larger batching window for better throughput). Ops will push back on per-route SLOs though.
Marcus: Ops will hate per-route SLOs. Alternative: have Optimize auto-propose batching/window settings and add a Console flag to accept. That keeps runtime static but surfaced.
Anya: Proposed action items:
- add pad_profile to manifest + intake validation
- adapt bench/admit to use pad_profile for sampling and gating
- surface Optimize suggestions in Console (batch/window) rather than hard SLOs
I'll draft a short RFC this week. Any blockers?
ingest-bot: Task created: IN-4921 "support pad_profile manifest + bench/admit changes"
PJ: :thumbsup: Ping me when RFC is up, happy to review.
